properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OkHttp CertificatePinner support wired into every generated REST client: ClientConfiguration holds a CertificatePinner field (getter/setter) and ApiClient applies it to the OkHttpClient builder at lines 181-182. Pinning constrains trust to classical X.509 / RSA / ECDSA keys, so the pinned material is quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks the underlying signature keys); pins must be re-cut when the service migrates certs. Changeable here — it is this library's configuration surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed Ed25519 PKCS#8 private keys (test-ed25519-prv-key.pem) under src/test/resources of five client modules, used by unit tests to exercise the Ed25519 request-signing path (PrivateKey/Ed25519 sign). Deliberately-public test fixtures, not production secrets — but they are real committed key material and the Ed25519 signature primitive they carry is Shor-vulnerable (deadline migration to ML-DSA, not harvest-urgent).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcpkix-jdk18on 1.84 (compile scope, clients/pom.xml ~382-386) provides the X.509/PEM machinery the connector actively uses in main code: JcaPEMKeyConverter/PrivateKeyInfo/PrivateKeyFactory in sign/PrivateKey.java for request-signing keys, and CertificateFactory.getInstance("X.509") + KeyStore CA loading in ApiClient.applySslSettings (ApiClient.java ~1770-1783). Also relevant: maven-gpg-plugin 3.2.4 is configured with <signer>bc</signer> (pom ~line 68) to GPG-sign release artifacts via Bouncy Cas

properties.name: pqs:context

No CMS call site exists in the application — bcpkix is pulled for its PKCS#8/PEM key handling (sign/PrivateKey.java), not CMS. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcpkix-jdk18on 1.84 is the crypto backbone of every module (compile scope, clients/pom.xml ~382-386): Ed25519Signer, RSADigestSigner, SHA256Digest, PrivateKeyFactory, JcaPEMKeyConverter, JceOpenSSLPKCS8DecryptorProviderBuilder and BouncyCastleProvider (registered into the JCA registry at sign/PrivateKey.java:64). BC 1.84 itself ships post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM/ML-DSA), but the connector's API surface exposes only the classical Ed25519/RSA/HMAC-SHA256 paths. Changeable here.
